definitions.planned: case x repetition units in the frozen plan set
definitions.attempted: units whose execution started: evaluable, unknown, or stopped there
definitions.evaluable: units with an enforced trajectory and recorded evaluator outcomes
definitions.unknown: recorded enforced trajectories whose evaluator outcome a bound annotation declares unknown
definitions.incomplete: the unit where the run stopped; evaluators were not reported

unknown.reason: matched/1 rows carry Boolean evaluator outputs only; the producer reports no unknown outcome. Ask (approval_required) is reported separately and is not unknown.

method.statistics: agentdojo_protocol.distribution: n, min, max; median = middle value, or the mean of the two middle values when n is even; p95 = nearest rank, the value at rank ceil(0.95 * n) of the sorted sample
method.measured: a recorded enforced trajectory carries its durations whether its evaluator outcome is known or declared unknown; an unknown evaluator outcome does not invalidate the recorded duration
method.not_measured: stopped units have no recorded duration (the producer reports none for the stopped attempt) and not-run units have none; they are counted, never imputed and never treated as censored measurements

limitations: Development comparison of recorded runs; not held-out efficacy, general safety or pilot readiness evidence.
Revision pins and the run's source inventory hash are producer declarations; this tool checks their consistency, not which binary or policy actually executed.

Input binding checks the identity of the supplied inputs, not that the producer executed them. Per-case full input, label and family are verified only through a case manifest inside the inventoried source; without one that link stays unverified (genuine upstream AgentDojo has none).

Paired differences and their family-cluster intervals are conditional on units evaluable in both runs; with partial coverage only the missing-outcome bounds on the planned set account for missing outcomes, and those bounds are not confidence intervals.

Family-cluster intervals treat resampling units as independent and exchangeable draws from the families of interest; they are approximate percentile intervals that tend to be too narrow with few clusters, and none is reported below the effective-cluster minimum. They describe this development set, not held-out performance.
Without declared semantic families no uncertainty is computed; correlated variants are then grouped by known plan dependencies only.
Unknown outcomes are unavailable in this producer contract; timeouts are not distinguishable.
Latency is descriptive and states no speed-up or slow-down.
